opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049) is a full-time Analyst. Requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is the maximum level for non-owners of the system; the request is at the maximum and is approved.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Recommended level: read.
reason: The two notes about E049 conflict: HR note says full-time Analyst (max write for Source Code), while Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read, never admin). Given the contradicting employment-type facts, I choose the level that is compliant under both interpretations: read is allowed for a full-time employee (at or below write max) and is exactly the maximum for a contractor with basic training. I cannot grant write because it would violate policy if the contractor record is correct, so the safe grant is read.
